title: Implement provider-neutral rule and judgment interfaces
summary: Create one evaluator contract for deterministic functions and future semantic providers. Make unknown, disagreement, and execution failure explicit so downstream policy cannot mistake unavailable judgment for no important concern.
in_scope: Immutable rule definitions and binding registry
Deterministic adapter and recorded external results
implementation: Implement versioned proposition, eligibility, precondition, and output-implication definitions.
Expose a binding interface that returns receipts and proposals without mutable core access.
Separate execution_status, evaluation_status, semantic_output, and qualification_status.
Validate output labels, cited IDs, admissible states, and consequence permissions before downstream use.

acceptance.criterion: A timeout cannot satisfy a negative semantic prerequisite.
acceptance.verification: Feed a fake timeout into a required downstream judgment.

acceptance.criterion: Deterministic and recorded semantic bindings share one neutral input contract.
acceptance.verification: Run packet validation through both bindings without application fields.

acceptance.criterion: Unknown output labels and nonexistent evidence IDs are refused.
acceptance.verification: Exercise structurally plausible but semantically invalid responses.

tests: Insufficient evidence may be completed execution with no conclusion.
A qualified score cannot grant transition authority.
Independent partial results survive another component failing.
A real control cancellation during evaluation removes the semantic output at the post gate.
A persisted upstream result retains its original target control context even when a fresh downstream token has the same epoch number.
A qualified recorded response cannot bypass an assessment permission denial.
A read denial blocks a new evaluator packet while preserving existing source history.
risks: A single success boolean would erase distinctions required for honest composition.

reuse.application: Use focused questions and qualification as provider-neutral evaluator concepts.

They exercise post-binding cancellation, stale original upstream control context despite a fresh equal-epoch downstream token, assessment denial before invoking a qualified recorded binding, and permission-checked source refusal with historical records retained.

AC-1: a timed-out attempt has no semantic conclusion and cannot satisfy a negative prerequisite. Insufficient evidence and not-applicable remain distinct completed outcomes; ambiguity and conflict remain inspectable. Independent successful bundles survive another failed attempt. Post-gate cancellation/currentness refusal preserves earlier stage events without allowing a failed callback to publish output.

AC-2: deterministic and recorded semantic bindings consume the same neutral ordered input contract, bound to the full immutable rule, exact binding, proposition, subject revision, evidence/locator snapshots, coverage and omissions, context, knowledge cut, dependencies and original control identity. Exact-recorded lookup refuses changed order or material input. Callbacks receive detached JSON without a supplied mutable core handle.

AC-3: fresh and consumed results use the same exact output-schema, label/status, evidence-ID/locator and permitted-proposal validation. Tests refuse unknown labels, invented citations, changed locators, undeclared proposals, wrong original input/subject mappings, and future-produced knowledge. Qualification binds exact schemas, preparation, rule, binding, task, threshold and actual-time validity; unknown certificates never become qualified and a qualified score grants no action authority.

Independent read-only review reproduced and verified fixes for external schema child rebinding, local-pointer escapes through annotation data, future result admission, invented consumed citations, undeclared consumed proposals, direct predecessor deadlines and original control contexts. Self-contained schemas resolve in isolated registries while valid local definitions and source fields named $ref/$id remain supported. No remaining blocker was identified within the bounded interface scope.

2026-10-10: generated-file checks, repository validation, all three synthetic walkthroughs, portable JavaScript vectors and whitespace checks passed. Validation reports 80 tickets, 104 requirements, 40 schemas, three walkthroughs and zero errors. The portable inventory remains 12 record kinds, 24 commands, 45 success pairs and 19 errors. Detailed local acceptance evidence is docs/validation/MAT-012.md.

Qualification is synthetic and bounded. The host authenticates configuration, policies, schema/adapter declarations and certificates, supplies authorized consistent snapshots and explicit prerequisite mappings, retains original control contexts, and owns atomic publication. The callback limit is cooperative after synchronous return, not preemptive execution or a process/memory sandbox. No certificate issuance/accuracy, provider quality, durable input restoration, transitive invalidation, native delivery, deployment or live attention usefulness is claimed.
